messages.subject: encoding error on upload of Shiny App--related to earlier questions from Windows users?
parts:
I am getting an encoding error on upload of a shiny app to ShinyApps.io.  App works locally on a Windows 7 SP Pro machine.   Trying to understand if I have a character string that is causing the error, since ShinyApps.io flags an error at the start of a line that is calling a character list defined in global environment:    selectInput("choose_var",label="Choose variable",choices=list_vars1).   The object list_vars1 is derived from a CSV file, read in with colClasses="character" option.  (See below for exact error)

I have read the article http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/unicode.html but not quite sure how to proceed.   Do I have to somehow adjust the encoding of the list object?  I saved the script files with encoding UTF-8 but that made no difference to the error message.

Thank you.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] encoding error on upload of Shiny App--related to earlier questions from Windows users?
parts:
Hi Kevin,

I looked into this issue and it turns out that it has nothing to do
with encoding. The current error message is too vague about where
exactly the error comes from. I just added a more informative message
to shinyapps. After you devtools::install_github('rstudio/shinyapps'),
you will realize the real problem:

Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading application bundle...

* Failed to parse /home/yihui/tmp/shiny-app2-master/scratch 16 Aug 2014.R

Error in parse(input, n = -1L, encoding = checkEncoding(file)) :
11:7: unexpected symbol
10: sidebarPanel
11: selectInput
^

Calls: <Anonymous> ... append -> fileDependencies ->
withCallingHandlers -> parse
Execution halted


So the problem is that you have an R script 'scratch 16 Aug 2014.R'
that is not a syntactically valid script. The reason that shinyapps
tries to parse this R script is that it actually parses all R scripts
in the app to figure out the package dependencies (e.g. you might have
library(foo) in bar.R and you source('bar.R') in server.R).

You can either remove this invalid R script from your app, or make it
a syntactically valid script.

Regards,
Yihui
